Two-panel comparison

Click an orbital lobe or choose a direction to highlight the corresponding P–Cl bond.

demo_steps.title: Two axial positions
demo_steps.narration: The upper and lower directions are highlighted in both panels. These are the two axial P-Cl bonds in the molecule and the two axial sp3d lobes in the orbital diagram.

demo_steps.narration: The three remaining directions form the equatorial set around the phosphorus center. The same three-direction arrangement appears in the molecular model and in the orbital diagram.

demo_steps.title: Bond-orbital correspondence
demo_steps.narration: Each P-Cl bond direction in panel (a) is matched by one sp3d hybrid orbital lobe in panel (b). Together, the five hybrid orbitals account for the trigonal bipyramidal bonding pattern in PCl5.

plan.geometry_notes: Use a shared trigonal bipyramidal coordinate system for both panels. Place panel (a) center near x=-2.4 and panel (b) center near x=+2.4, with both structures scaled to about 2.8 units tall so they fill the frame together. Let axial directions be (0, +1, 0) and (0, -1, 0). Let equatorial directions be (1, 0, 0), (-0.5, 0, +0.866), and (-0.5, 0, -0.866). Pre-rotate both groups slightly about the vertical axis, about -20 degrees, so one equatorial direction projects prominently to the right while the axial pair remains visually vertical, matching the source orientation. Panel (a): phosphorus radius about 0.28 units, chlorine radius about 0.34 units, P-Cl center distance about 1.25 units, bond cylinder radius about 0.055 units. Phosphorus color orange #d96f1f; chlorine color green #3bb64a with lighter highlight #7ed957; bonds can be neutral gray #b8b8b8 or subtly split orange/green if matching the source rendering. Panel (b): central nucleus black #111111, radius about 0.09 units; each sp3d lobe is a teardrop or elongated ellipsoid about 1.15 units long and 0.42 units wide, colored warm yellow-orange #f7b447 with darker orange edge/shadow #e68a25. Place the five lobe tips along the same five direction vectors. Dashed trigonal-bipyramid outline in olive green #7aa33a: connect the three equatorial tips to form a dashed triangle and connect each axial tip to each equatorial tip. Five italic black 'sp3d' labels must be visible in the default render, offset just outside each lobe tip so they do not overlap the lobes.
plan.notes: Render both panels simultaneously in one scene; do not use a view selector or mode switch. Keep the initial camera/static composition close to the source: panel (a) on the left, panel (b) on the right, axial directions vertical on screen, and enough horizontal spacing that labels in panel (b) are not clipped. Do not render angle guide arcs or 90/120 degree labels. Use CSS2DRenderer or sprite text for '(a)', '(b)', and all five 'sp3d' labels so they remain readable. OrbitControls should rotate the two panel groups in sync around their own centers or around a shared midpoint, with a reset-to-default view available in the implementation if possible. Click picking should map each chlorine/bond/lobe to one of the five shared direction indices and apply corresponding highlight halos in both panels. Guided focus states should add translucent halos or brighter outlines only; the base textbook figure should remain visible underneath.

authoredPrompt: This figure contains two panels, (a) and (b), illustrating sp3d hybridization in phosphorus pentachloride (PCl5) at the molecular and orbital levels. Panel (a) shows a ball-and-stick model of PCl5 with an orange phosphorus atom at the center covalently bonded to five green chlorine atoms directed toward the vertices of a trigonal bipyramid: two axial Cl atoms situated above and below the central P atom along a vertical axis, and three equatorial Cl atoms arranged symmetrically in the horizontal plane. Panel (b) depicts the five sp3d hybrid orbitals that account for these five bonds, each shown as a large orange lobe radiating from a central black dot representing the phosphorus nucleus, labeled "sp3d," and arranged in the same trigonal bipyramidal pattern with dashed lines connecting the lobe tips to outline the geometry; small back-lobes are omitted for clarity. This figure establishes sp3d hybridization — derived from mixing one 3s, three 3p, and one 3d orbital of phosphorus — as the valence-bond explanation for the five equivalent bonding regions in PCl5 and connects orbital theory directly to the observed trigonal bipyramidal molecular structure.
authoredInteractions:
- Toggle between the ball-and-stick molecular model (panel a) and the sp3d hybrid orbital lobe diagram (panel b): compare the physical geometry of bonds to the underlying orbital shapes
- Rotate the 3D trigonal bipyramidal structure: distinguish axial from equatorial positions and confirm the 90 degree and 120 degree bond angles
- Click any hybrid orbital lobe in panel (b): highlight the corresponding bond direction in the molecular model panel (a)
authoredContext:
In a molecule of phosphorus pentachloride, PCl 5 , there are five P–Cl bonds (thus five pairs of valence electrons around the phosphorus atom) directed toward the corners of a trigonal bipyramid. We use the 3 s orbital, the three 3 p orbitals, and one of the 3 d orbitals to form the set of five sp 3 d hybrid orbitals ( ) that are involved in the P–Cl bonds. Other atoms that exhibit sp 3 d hybridization include the sulfur atom in SF 4 and the chlorine atoms in ClF 3 and in ClF 4 + . (The electrons on fluorine atoms are omitted for clarity.)

(a) The five regions of electron density around phosphorus in PCl 5 require five hybrid sp 3 d orbitals. (b) These orbitals combine to form a trigonal bipyramidal structure with each large lobe of the hybrid orbital pointing at a vertex. As before, there are also small lobes pointing in the opposite direction for each orbital (not shown for clarity).

Two images are shown and labeled “a” and “b.” Image a depicts a ball-and-stick model in a trigonal bipyramidal arrangement. Image b depicts the hybrid orbitals in the same arrangement and each is labeled, “s p superscript three d.”

The sulfur atom in sulfur hexafluoride, SF 6 , exhibits sp 3 d 2 hybridization. A molecule of sulfur hexafluoride has six bonding pairs of electrons connecting six fluorine atoms to a single sulfur atom. There are no lone pairs of electrons on the central atom. To bond six fluorine atoms, the 3 s orbital, the three 3 p orbitals, and two of the 3 d orbitals form six equivalent sp 3 d 2 hybrid orbitals, each directed toward a different corner of an octahedron. Other atoms that exhibit sp 3 d 2 hybridization include the phosphorus atom in PCl 6 − , the iodine atom in the interhalogens IF 6 + , IF 5 , ICl 4 − , IF 4 − and the xenon atom in XeF 4 .

interactionPlan.geometry_notes: Use a trigonal bipyramidal coordinate system centered at phosphorus. Approximate scale: P atom radius 0.32 units; Cl atom radius 0.42 units; P-Cl bond length about 1.65 units from P center to Cl center; bond cylinder radius about 0.09 units. Let the axial directions be (0, 0, +1) and (0, 0, -1). Let the three equatorial directions be (1, 0, 0), (-1/2, +sqrt(3)/2, 0), and (-1/2, -sqrt(3)/2, 0), then rotate the whole object so one axial bond appears vertical on screen and one equatorial bond projects to the right as in the source. Colors: phosphorus orange #d96f1f, chlorine green #36b84a with lighter highlights #7ed957, bonds orange/green split near atoms, orbital lobes warm yellow-orange #f7b447 with darker orange outline #e68a25 and translucent fill, dashed guide lines olive green #7aa33a, central nucleus black #111111, labels black. Panel (b) lobes should be elongated teardrop/ellipsoid forms about 1.25 units long and 0.55 units wide, with tips at the same five trigonal bipyramidal directions. Small opposite back-lobes are omitted, matching the source. Angle guides: axial-equatorial = 90 degrees; equatorial-equatorial = 120 degrees.
interactionPlan.notes: Implement the two panels as two alternative scene layers sharing the same underlying five direction vectors, not as separate layouts. The view toggle should fade between layers while preserving camera orientation and any selected direction. Use OrbitControls with limited zoom and no roll; keep labels screen-facing using CSS2D or sprite text. For orbital lobes, use scaled metaball-like meshes, elongated ellipsoids, or custom lathed teardrop geometry aligned to each direction vector. Use dashed LineSegments for the green trigonal bipyramid outline in panel (b). Click picking should work on orbital lobe meshes in the sp3d view and store a selected direction index; in the molecular view, apply a bright outline or glow to the corresponding bond cylinder and chlorine atom.

discrepancies: The source shows two panels side by side, ball-and-stick (a) and orbital diagram (b), but the generated figure shows only one panel at a time and the initial view entirely omits panel (b).
The generated ball-and-stick panel includes 90° and 120° angle guide arcs and labels that are not present in the source figure.

The overall composition is not faithful: the source has the molecule on the left and the orbital sketch on the right with matching scale, while the generated model is centered as a single large object with UI-driven switching.
The sp3d labels and orbital lobes are absent from the rendered initial screenshot, whereas they are prominent in the source.
The molecular model viewpoint differs enough that the trigonal-bipyramidal arrangement is less like the reference, with the rear/left equatorial positions appearing crowded behind the axial bond.
evaluation.notes: The molecular geometry is mostly correct and the interactions are useful, but the figure is not faithful to the original two-panel composition and adds non-source angle annotations.

Remove the 90° and 120° angle guide arcs and labels unless explicitly requested, since they do not appear in the source.
Adjust the initial camera and object placement so the ball-and-stick model matches the source orientation and left-panel placement more closely.
Ensure the five sp3d labels are visible with the orbital panel in the default rendered figure.
